transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-22 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~46 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Lina Cho (Redwood SE), Mark Reynolds (Arden Head of Platform), Priya Nair (Arden ML Lead), Jorge Alvarez (Arden CISO)

Summary:
Quick intro, high-level constraints (latency SLOs, multilingual support), dive on context length needs (8k vs 32k), open-model comparisons for cost/quality, tool-calling support (internal search + ticketing integration), and deployment options (hosted vs dedicated vs private VPC). Agreed to run benchmarks and share pricing & security docs.

Topics:
- Current infra & pain points (on-prem latency, bursty peak loads)
- Model selection: open models vs managed LLMs
- Context length and KV cache behavior
- Tool-calling: connectors to internal search, DB, and ticketing system
- Security/compliance: SOC2, SSO, KMS, audit logs

Action items (recap at end included above)

Transcript body:
[00:00] Samir: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Samir from Redwood, I'm the AE on this. With me is Lina, our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing?
[00:12] Mark: Good, thanks. We — yeah we're excited, been looking at options for inference for a while.
[00:18] Priya: Hi, Priya here. We've been testing some open models in-house but running into cost and latency trade-offs when we push context longer than 8k.
[00:26] Jorge: Jorge from security also on. I'll mostly listen but will flag anything about encryption or auditability.
[00:31] Lina: Great, quick agenda, we'll ask about your stack, walk through model options (open vs hosted), context/throughput implications, and then tool-calling/connectors. Sound ok?
[00:40] Mark: Yep, go for it.

[01:05] Lina: Priya, can you describe the main workload? You mentioned longer contexts — is it multi-document summarization, retrieval-augmented generation, or chat?
[01:12] Priya: It's mostly RAG for customer support transcripts plus live operator assist. So we need the model to ingest up to a day's convo for context — sometimes that's 10–12k tokens, other times enterprise contracts and email threads push toward 25–30k. Our current ops cost with the open model stack is spiking when we do 32k windows.
[01:35] Samir: Understood. That pushes into two decisions: model architecture/size and deployment mode. For long context you'd pick either model variants with native long-context (like some trimmed attention models) or use windowing + smarter retrieval + Redwood's prefix/KV caching to reduce tokens per request.
[01:55] Priya: Can you tell us more about the caching? We've seen 'KV cache' mentioned in docs but unclear how the runtime manages multi-user caches and cost accounting.
[02:05] Lina: Sure. Our runtime does adaptive prefix caching — for repeated histories we keep the KV cache in memory on the serving instance so subsequent requests use fewer compute ops for the prefix tokens. It also supports cache invalidation policies per-customer. For cost accounting, we give token-level breakdowns in the Console so you can see whether cost is from prefix reuse or new generation.
[02:29] Mark: That sounds helpful. But in terms of SLA, we have <150ms token latency SLO for assist features. Is that realistic with 40B models and caching?
[02:40] Lina: For single-token latencies, with dedicated GPU pools and optimized kernels we can get low per-token latencies, often <100ms on T4/RTX-class for smaller models; with 40B and 32k context, performance depends on sequence length and batching. If you need consistent sub-150ms at scale, Redwood Dedicated with pinned capacity is the safer bet. Hosted can be fast but the variability increases with multi-tenant bursts.
[03:05] Priya: So Dedicated for predictability, hosted for faster ramp. What about Private VPC? We need to keep PII on-prem for certain contracts.
[03:14] Samir: Private option gives you a customer-managed control plane and VPC peering or even on-prem package. That includes KMS integration; you keep keys. You also get audit logs and can configure retention. There's an enterprise contract for Private.
[03:28] Jorge: On KMS, must the model weights or logs ever leave our network? What's the guarantee?
[03:34] Lina: For Private deployments, the runtime and model weights can be hosted in your VPC or on-prem; logs can be forwarded to your SIEM. Hosted/Dedicated send telemetry to Redwood but you can opt for minimal telemetry and long-term audit export. We'll share the security whitepaper with details.
[03:52] Mark: Awesome. Back to models — which open models do you recommend for our mixture of RAG + tool-calling? We want strong instruction following, multilingual (EN/ES/PT), and decent hallucination behavior.
[04:05] Lina: For that mix, teams often test a family: LLaMA-derived 13B/30B, a 40B quantized variant that balances quality/latency, and some of the newer long-context models. For multilingual, make sure you evaluate on your Spanish/Portuguese sets — some models drop off. Redwood Optimize can run scoring across your prompt sets to recommend the best candidate.
[04:28] Priya: Do you do automated evals? We have a few hundred evaluation prompts.
[04:33] Samir: Yes, we can run Redwood Optimize evals and give model recommendations tied to cost/latency trade-offs. Lina will pick up the eval config.

[05:02] Priya: Tool-calling — we need to call internal search (Elasticsearch), a ticket system (Jira), and an internal billing DB for account lookups. How do you handle connectors / credentials?
[05:12] Lina: We provide a tool-calling surface—function calling style. For Hosted, you can register webhook endpoints or a connector in the Console; secrets are stored in our KMS but if you're on Private you can store keys in your KMS/HSM. Our runtime serializes tool outputs and can do structured outputs to minimize hallucination.
[05:33] Jorge: Any posture on data ex-filtration? We're paranoid about models returning raw snippets of PII.
[05:38] Lina: There are several layers: redaction in preprocessing, enforcement policies on response tokens, and the option to keep tool outputs internal (not stored) so they don't get into logs. We can also configure prompt filters to scrub PII before sending to the model.

[06:10] Mark: Let's talk numbers: rough per-token cost for hosted vs dedicated for the 40B quant model? Even a ballpark helps.
[06:17] Samir: Ballpark — hosted is higher due to multi-tenant. Say hosted generation unit equivalent of X per 1k tokens, dedicated drops unit cost 30–60% depending on committed capacity and batching. Exact numbers depend on utilization — we'll put a pricing matrix in the follow-up.
[06:33] Priya: If we go dedicated, what commit levels and scaling patterns do you expect? Our traffic is bursty around product launches.
[06:40] Lina: We support configurable autoscaling with reserved baseline and burst buckets. You can set policy thresholds for queue depth or latency, and Redwood can burst into spare capacity for short periods. For long bursts, dedicated pool needs capacity. We'll recommend commit tiers based on your P95 RPS and target latency.

[07:05] Priya: I'm curious about token accounting when we use retrieval — do you count retrieved docs as input tokens?
[07:10] Lina: Yes, anything that goes into the model context counts for token accounting. That’s why prefix caching and retrieval summarization helps reduce billed tokens. We also surface per-request breakdown in the Console so you can track it.

[08:00] Mark: Let's sketch a pilot: 2-week RAG benchmark, run on dedicated trial capacity for your 40B quant model, measure latency at 8k and 32k, measure cost per convo, and run the multilingual evaluation. Does that sound reasonable?
[08:12] Samir: That's perfect. Lina will run initial throughput estimates and we'll schedule a benchmarking window.
[08:18] Priya: For the benchmarking, can we use our data? Some of it is PII so we'd need Private or a dedicated environment with strict retention.
[08:27] Samir: We can run benchmarks in a Private trial if needed. Otherwise for hosted/dedicated we have redaction flows. We'll work with Jorge on the security constraints.

[09:00] Jorge: Quick question on compliance: do you provide SOC2 Type II reports and support for ISO audits?
[09:06] Samir: Yes, Redwood has SOC2 Type II. For Private deployments we provide the platform artifacts to support your ISO audits and can do on-site reviews with enterprise support. We'll share the attestation.

[10:10] Priya: Any gotchas on multilingual tokenization? For instance our Spanish transcripts have long word tokens; cost estimates shifted when we tested due to different tokenization patterns.
[10:21] Lina: Tokenization differences are real. For Spanish/Portuguese you might see slight token inflation but most modern open models are trained multilingual enough. We'll run your sample set through the tokenizer to give adjusted token estimates.

[12:00] Mark: What about model rollouts and A/B tests? We need a canary path for new model versions without disrupting production.
[12:07] Lina: Redwood Console supports per-route model pinning, canary rollouts, and automatic fallback policies. If a new model regresses on quality or latency, you can auto-fallback to a previous variant. You can also do percentage-based traffic splits.

[14:00] Priya: For tool-calling reliability, how do you ensure that a tool failure doesn't cause a bad user experience?
[14:06] Lina: We have retry/backoff policies and a fallback chain: if internal search times out, we can fall back to a cached snippet or a lighter heuristic. You configure the policy per-tool. We also surface tool latencies and error rates in the Console.

[17:30] Mark: Are there model variants that truly handle 32k natively or will we be forced into retrieval windowing?
[17:36] Lina: Some recent long-context variants do native 32k with optimized attention kernels, but they are larger and more expensive. Often a hybrid of retrieval+longer context model is cost-effective—keep the KV cache warm for conversation history and only bring in long documents when needed.
[18:05] Priya: For hallucinations, have you done work on model/regression alerts?
[18:12] Samir: Yes, Redwood Optimize includes quality monitoring tied to prompt sets and evals. You can create regression alerts when a model's score drops on your test prompts compared to the baseline.

[22:00] Jorge: Regarding keys and secrets: if we go Dedicated, can we integrate our HSM for signing?
[22:06] Lina: For Private we support HSM/KMS integrations. For Dedicated we can offer customer-owned KMS for certain flows or a bring-your-own-key approach for sensitive tokens. We will validate integration options during the pilot scoping.

[26:00] Mark: Any reference customers in telecom or real-time assist?
[26:05] Samir: We have a couple; I'll include anonymized case studies — one on low-latency assist and one on RAG for customer support.

[30:00] Priya: One more technical: batching strategy — if we have many small interactive requests, does Redwood aggressively batch? That could increase latency.
[30:09] Lina: Batching is adaptive; we do tiny-request fast-paths to avoid adding latency for interactive flows, and continuous batching for background jobs. You set latency targets, and the runtime chooses batching heuristics to meet SLOs.

[34:00] Mark: Ok logistics — timeline and stakeholders. We're aiming for a Q3 pilot but want procurement/compliance in May. Who from Redwood does procurement work with?
[34:09] Samir: I'll own the procurement loop. We'll share standard terms and an enterprise addendum for Private deployments. Legal and procurement often run in parallel with the pilot if you're comfortable.

[38:00] Priya: For the sample eval, we'll provide 300 utterances in English, 150 in Spanish and 50 in Portuguese. Expect some noise.
[38:09] Samir: Perfect, send them to samir@redwood.ai. We'll run them through Optimize and return a model ranking plus cost/latency tradeoffs.

[40:00] Jorge: I'm going to send the security spreadsheet — network zones, required certs, and data flow diagrams. Expect details on key custody and log retention.
[40:07] Samir: Great. We'll review and circle back with Lina on feasibility for a Private pilot.

[42:00] Recap / Next steps:
- Samir: Share Dedicated/Private pricing matrix, security whitepaper, and anonymized telecom case studies (by 2026-04-24)
- Lina: Run throughput/latency estimates and configure Redwood Optimize eval for provided sample prompts (deliver by 2026-04-29)
- Priya: Upload sample datasets and desired SLOs (by 2026-04-24)
- Jorge: Share security spreadsheet with network & KMS requirements (by 2026-04-25)

[45:10] Mark: Thanks all — this was super helpful. We'll sync once we get the docs and set a time for the deep technical bench.
[45:20] Samir: Thanks everyone, appreciate it.
[45:30] Meeting end.
